summary: builder-II's demo surface has one genuinely operational flagship — the CORE demo loop (builder_ii/core_demo_loop.py, promoted OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED, mapped to DEMO_ONLY_VERIFIED assurance) which really does prepare a detached git worktree, emit a digest-bound HITL proposal/approval, apply a patch, verify, roll back, and chain-verify evidence — plus a read-only CodeVault determinism demo (builder_ii/code_vault_demo_loop.py) with three real in-memory proofs and a clean read-only TUI (code_vault_tui.py). Everything else is artifact-only or recital: readonly_founder_demo.py writes planning JSON without executing anything, target_profile_demos.py just prints command recipes, and operator_golden_path.py generates status reports "without execution." The two biggest problems for a skeptical-senior-engineer audience are (1) the flagship mutation demo is hard-wired to AssetOverflow/core (repo-name/remote check, hard-coded marker patch, CORE-specific protected-module list) so no "bring your own repo" equivalent exists even though the underlying primitives (hitl_patch_proposal/apply/rollback, postflight records) are already generic; and (2) the showcase STRATUM Textual TUI (builder_ii/tui/app.py) contains admitted mockup behavior — fake tier evaluation, fabricated chain digest, notify-only HITL approve/reject that writes no artifacts, a CLI passthrough that doesn't execute, and a Swift-subprocess splash whose tagline ("CORE-native governed AI platform") contradicts the generic-first doctrine. There are zero recorded assets (no GIF/asciinema/video anywhere; images/ holds one splash JPEG). A strong 15-minute narrative is constructible today entirely from promoted capabilities: operator status → phase-by-phase CORE demo loop with live git-status proofs → deliberate report tampering caught by validate-demo-loop's digest check → CodeVault determinism proofs — but it needs a generic-target variant, a scripted flagship doc, and recorded media to travel beyond the founder's machine.
current_state: CORE demo loop (builder_ii/core_demo_loop.py, 984 lines) is a real end-to-end governed loop: creates a detached git worktree from CORE HEAD (_prepare_worktree, lines 207-215), writes preflight/repo-map/context-pack/deterministic-planner/HITL patch proposal, requires an approval artifact binding the exact patch SHA-256 (create_core_demo_approval, lines 326-363), applies via apply_hitl_patch, emits before/after verification receipts checking the marker AND that CORE sensitive modules are untouched (lines 540-601), rolls back via rollback_hitl_patch, writes a final clean postflight that raises if the worktree is dirty (lines 604-625), and finalizes with chain verification + artifact index + DEMO_EVIDENCE.md (lines 811-840).

The CORE demo loop is promoted OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED in builder_ii/platform_completion_audit.py (capability row 'CORE demo loop', ~line 863) but its assurance is explicitly downgraded to DEMO_ONLY_VERIFIED (lines 150-151: `if row.capability == "CORE demo loop": return DEMO_ONLY_VERIFIED`). CLI surfaces builder-platform demo-loop / validate-demo-loop / wow exist in builder_ii/cli/platform_status_cli.py (lines 217, 270, 297) and are tested end-to-end against a real temp git repo in tests/test_core_demo_loop.py (test_core_demo_all_applies_verifies_rolls_back_and_indexes_evidence).

The CORE demo loop is CORE-specific by construction: _ensure_core_repo (core_demo_loop.py lines 192-204) rejects any repo whose remotes lack 'AssetOverflow/core' unless the directory is literally named 'core'; the patch is a hard-coded doc marker (_DEMO_MARKER_PATH, _unified_diff_for_marker, lines 49, 224-249); the planner and verification receipts hard-code CORE's sensitive-module list (algebra/, field/, vault/, etc., lines 281-290 and 566-577); artifact kinds are builder_ii.core_demo_* (lines 21-27).

The underlying primitives the CORE demo uses are already generic: _write_patch_proposal calls create_hitl_patch_proposal(target_name="generic", ...) then relabels the target to 'core' (core_demo_loop.py lines 309-323); _write_final_postflight does the same (lines 604-617). Per platform_completion_audit.py, 'HITL patch application' and 'rollback execution' capabilities are MERGED_BUT_NOT_OPERATIONAL ('remains gated/unpromoted'), and builder-hitl apply-patch is TIER_3 / STATE_HITL_RUNTIME_CANDIDATE in builder_ii/command_authority.py (lines 2267-2280) — so the full patch loop is only promoted inside the CORE demo lane.

CodeVault determinism demo (builder_ii/code_vault_demo_loop.py) executes three real in-memory proofs (replay_identical_frame, sibling_addition_preserves_anchor, content_edit_changes_digest_not_center; _run_determinism_proofs lines 143-236), emits a chained read-only artifact bundle, cross-checks the replay digest against the emitted frame (lines 433-436), and is documented for recording in docs/demos/CODE_VAULT_DETERMINISM_DEMO.md with 8 recording beats and a governance on-camera script. docs/CODE_VAULT_STAGED_ACCEPTANCE.md line 50 classifies it 'artifact_only / validation_only ... Not promoted beyond recording eval'. CLI: builder-code-vault demo / validate-demo (builder_ii/cli/code_vault_cli.py lines 342, 371); tests exist (tests/test_code_vault_demo_loop.py, tests/test_code_vault_tui.py).

Read-only inspection TUIs are honest and tested: builder_ii/code_vault_tui.py (542 lines, 8 subcommands, all read from $BUILDER_DIR JSON, exit-code semantics on validation failure), builder_ii/goose_tui.py (801 lines, 7 read-only manifest commands), builder_ii/agent_tui.py (1173 lines, pure Rich renderers, zero subprocess use — grep confirmed 0 hits).

The readonly founder demo (builder_ii/readonly_founder_demo.py, exposed as builder-targets readonly-founder-demo in builder_ii/cli/targets_cli.py line 114) writes only passive planning artifacts (inspection plan, patch proposal, verification plan, event ledger with 4 events, replay report) with every authority DISABLED (get_forbidden_authority_boundaries, lines 33-44); it executes nothing. platform_completion_audit.py classifies it PASSIVE_FOUNDATION (lines 563-581).

target_profile_demos.py (148 lines) is pure declarative data — three TargetProfileDemo records (generic/builder/core) whose 'commands' are strings printed by builder-targets demo; 'no command execution is performed by the demo' (line 41). This is the only generic-target demo artifact and it is recital, not execution.

operator_golden_path.py generates operator-status.json + operator-next.json + a golden-path report with anti-truth-inflation validators (rejects exercised capabilities not OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED, lines 247-258; rejects empty known_gaps, lines 287-304) but its own warnings say 'Golden path demo generated without execution. No target repository mutation occurred.' (line 162). operator_status.py similarly emits STATUS_REPORT_ONLY digest-bound reports.

The STRATUM Textual TUI (builder_ii/tui/app.py, launched via `builder stratum`, builder_ii/cli/main.py lines 128-147) contains explicit mockup behavior: command palette uses 'Fake evaluation for UI demo' (line 306), chain digest is fabricated ('Fake a digest for display', lines 247-249), CLI passthrough only notifies ('Real implementation would subprocess run', lines 337-344), diff action says 'Diff view not yet available in this mockup' (line 613), HITL approve/reject write no approval artifacts (lines 572-605), and show_hitl_gate (stratum.py line 568) has zero callers outside the widget itself. Splash/branding: builder_ii/tui/widgets/splash.py compiles-and-runs an embedded Swift/Cocoa program via `swift` subprocess at TUI startup to float images/builder-ii-splash-hero.jpeg (the only image asset in the repo) over the desktop for 4 seconds (lines 60-120); the ASCII splash tagline reads 'CORE-native governed AI platform' (line 17), contradicting README.md line 12 ('builder-II itself is not CORE...'). Recording documentation exists but no recorded media does: docs/CORE_DEMO_WALKTHROUGH.md is a full narrated 6-phase recording script with talk tracks and terminal-proof beats; docs/OPERATOR_QUICKSTART.md wires golden path + demo loop; docs/demos/CODE_VAULT_DETERMINISM_DEMO.md has recording beats; core_demo_loop reports carry a ready_for_recording flag and DEMO_EVIDENCE.md lists 'Recording Beats' (core_demo_loop.py lines 758-765). A repo-wide find for *.gif/*.cast/*.mp4/*.mov/*.svg returned nothing; images/ contains only builder-ii-splash-hero.jpeg.

Demo determinism/safety hardening exists: readonly_founder_demo.validate_safe_demo_directory_for_deletion fail-closes --force deletion to .builder/demos/ or scoped temp dirs (readonly_founder_demo.py lines 252-318); code_vault_demo_loop rejects dangerous output dirs and --force deletes only known filenames (lines 103-124); core demo report digests are validated (validate_core_demo_report checks report_digest against canonical content, lines 725-732), enabling a live tamper-detection beat.
gaps: No generic-target ('bring your own repo') flagship demo exists. The only demo that applies+rolls back a real patch is locked to AssetOverflow/core by _ensure_core_repo (builder_ii/core_demo_loop.py lines 192-204) and hard-coded CORE invariants (lines 281-290, 566-577). The generic target's only demo is a printed command recipe in builder_ii/target_profile_demos.py (lines 22-44, 'no command execution is performed'). A skeptical engineer cannot point builder-II at their own repo and feel the approve→apply→verify→rollback loop.

Zero recorded presentation assets. find for .gif/.cast/.mp4/.mov/.svg across the repo returned nothing; images/ contains only builder-ii-splash-hero.jpeg. docs/CORE_DEMO_WALKTHROUGH.md and docs/demos/CODE_VAULT_DETERMINISM_DEMO.md are recording scripts with no recordings; README.md embeds only the splash JPEG.

STRATUM TUI is a partially non-functional mockup on the most visible surface: fake tier evaluation (builder_ii/tui/app.py line 306), fabricated chain digest (lines 247-249), notify-only HITL approve/reject producing no approval artifacts (lines 572-605), non-executing CLI passthrough (lines 337-344), 'not yet available in this mockup' diff (line 613), and show_hitl_gate never triggered from real proposal artifacts (no callers found). No StratumApp tests exist.

The HITL approval moment in the flagship demo is a CLI flag, not an interaction: approval is granted by re-running with --approve (builder_ii/cli/platform_status_cli.py lines 234-238; core_demo_loop.py lines 897-913). There is no interactive TTY prompt showing the diff and digest at the decision point, which weakens the 'governance felt, not recited' effect.

No single scripted 15-minute flagship document exists. docs/CORE_DEMO_WALKTHROUGH.md covers only the CORE loop; docs/OPERATOR_QUICKSTART.md covers golden path; docs/demos/CODE_VAULT_DETERMINISM_DEMO.md covers CodeVault. Nothing sequences them with timings, and no doc scripts the highest-impact beat available today: tampering with core-demo-loop-report.json and having builder-platform validate-demo-loop fail on report_digest mismatch (validator exists at core_demo_loop.py lines 725-732).

Branding/doctrine drift on the splash: tagline 'CORE-native governed AI platform' (builder_ii/tui/widgets/splash.py line 17) contradicts README.md line 12 and docs/demos/CORE_READONLY_FOUNDER_DEMO.md ('builder-II is not CORE'). The splash also compile-runs Swift via subprocess inside a TUI whose surrounding docs advertise 'no shell execution' lanes (splash.py lines 60-120) — macOS-only and a governance-optics liability.

Demo portability: docs/CORE_DEMO_WALKTHROUGH.md hard-codes /Users/kaizenpro/Projects/core (lines 24, 42+); `wow` without --approve silently degrades to phase=prepare only (platform_status_cli.py line 313), an easy live-demo footgun; readonly_founder_demo event records claim command_surface 'builder-targets generate-demo' (readonly_founder_demo.py lines 376, 413) while the actual CLI command is 'builder-targets readonly-founder-demo' (targets_cli.py line 114) — an evidence-vs-surface drift a skeptical reviewer would catch.

Recording retakes are not digest-reproducible: every CORE demo artifact embeds wall-clock created_at (core_demo_loop.py _utc_timestamp line 149) so all digests differ between takes; only the CodeVault frame_digest is replay-stable (code_vault_demo_loop.py lines 143-160). No option exists to pin timestamps for reproducible recording bundles.

risks: Audience credibility risk: if the STRATUM TUI is shown in its current state, a skeptical senior engineer pressing 'a' (approve) or '~' (CLI passthrough) will discover the actions are notify-only mockups with fake digests (builder_ii/tui/app.py lines 247-249, 306, 337-344, 572-613) inside a product whose entire pitch is 'artifacts over claims' — a direct contradiction of the governance story.

Portability risk: the only executing mutation demo requires an AssetOverflow/core checkout or a repo directory literally named 'core' (core_demo_loop.py lines 192-204) plus macOS/uv assumptions and founder-specific paths in docs — gift recipients cannot reproduce the flagship on their own repos without the generic loop work item.

Truth-inflation optics: 'CORE demo loop' is labeled OPERATIONALLY_VERIFIED in the capability matrix while the general 'HITL patch application' and 'rollback execution' capabilities remain MERGED_BUT_NOT_OPERATIONAL (platform_completion_audit.py); the assurance layer correctly downgrades it to DEMO_ONLY_VERIFIED, but a presenter who overstates the promoted scope invites exactly the skepticism the platform is designed to prevent.

Live-demo footguns: `wow` without --approve silently runs prepare-only; --force semantics differ across demos (worktree replacement vs known-filename deletion vs guarded rmtree); timestamps make retake digests differ, so a narrator claiming 'identical every run' would be wrong for everything except the CodeVault frame_digest.

Splash startup shells out to `swift` (compile+run) on every TUI launch (splash.py) — on machines without the Xcode toolchain this silently delays startup, and if noticed by the audience it undermines the 'no shell execution' branding of adjacent lanes.

Maintenance drift risk: three parallel demo families (CORE loop, readonly founder, CodeVault) with separate evidence formats and force/cleanup semantics already show drift (readonly founder demo's command_surface string names a nonexistent CLI command); adding a generic loop without consolidating conventions will widen this.
